subject: Request: availability target exception for AtlasHealth - order form language & MSA attachments
messages:
From: Nina Park <nina.park@atlashealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Availability target and order form language - AtlasHealth

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at AtlasHealth is moving fast but we need to confirm a couple of contract-level items before we can issue a PO. Specifically: 

- Availability: We need to see a written commitment to 99.95% monthly availability in the order form (we understand Redwood typically offers 99.9, but our compliance team requested that any exceptions be documented in the Order Form / Addendum).
- Latency objectives: Our SLOs require guidance for P95 inference latency for our production model (we're aiming for P95 <= 400ms on the hosted tier).
- Evidence: Please attach the redlined MSA you mentioned (Atlas team sent our version as Atlas_MSA_v3.pdf) and a draft Order Form with the proposed exception language so our legal can review.

Can you send a draft addendum/order-form snippet and confirm how availability will be measured and credited? Also include any carve-outs (maintenance windows, force majeure, known degradations) and the monitoring/alerting proofpoints.

We'd like to close this this week if possible.

Thanks,
Nina Park
Senior Procurement Manager | AtlasHealth
procurement@atlashealth.com

Attachment: Atlas_MSA_v3.pdf (received)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Availability target and order form language - AtlasHealth

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear ask and the MSA copy. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Laura (sales ops) to align on the order form language and any exceptions.

Quick answers up front:
- We can accommodate a documented availability exception in the Order Form/Annex with explicit measurement/calculation.
- For hosted customers we currently target 99.9% uptime; we can work with a 99.95% target for a scoped Order Form with explicit compensating credits and carve-outs.
- For P95 latency, we will include a target and monitoring spec but want to qualify that latency SLOs are dependent on model choice, input sizes, and region. We'll propose a measured P95 baseline across typical production traffic and an escalation path.

I'll pull together a draft addendum and a redlined Order Form snippet for legal review. Ben / Laura — are you okay with a short addendum that: (1) defines availability calculation (minutes of downtime per calendar month), (2) lists exclusions (scheduled maintenance windows; emergency mitigations), and (3) specifies credit tiers tied to monthly availability bands?

Chloe
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Availability target and order form language - AtlasHealth

Chloe / Laura — quick internal take from a commercial perspective:

I support offering a scoped Order Form addendum that sets the availability at 99.95% for the hosted API environment for their production tenant, with the following guardrails: 

- Availability measured as: (Total available minutes in month - minutes of unplanned outage impacting production requests) / Total available minutes in month.
- Credit structure (proposal):
  * >=99.95%: no credit
  * 99.0% - 99.949%: 10% service credit on monthly invoice
  * 97.0% - 98.999%: 25% service credit
  * <97.0%: 50% service credit or termination right after 2 consecutive months below 97%
- Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance (we'll define a 4-hour monthly maintenance window), DDOS mitigation, customer-caused incidents (misconfiguration/over-quota), and force majeure.
- Latency note: we can include a P95 guidance line (P95 <= 400ms) but phrase it as "performance objective" with a remediation path rather than hard credit. If they require latency credits we should escalate to commercial leadership.

Vivek — can you confirm operational feasibility for measuring availability at the tenant level and automating the monthly report we would provide? If we can include an automated monthly uptime report link in the Order Form, that will help legal and procurement.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Availability target and order form language - AtlasHealth

Ben / team — operationally this is doable with the following implementation details: 

- Tenant-level availability: we already emit per-tenant health metrics and can compute monthly uptime with our monitoring pipeline. We'll provide a signed monthly uptime report (CSV + dashboard link).
- Maintenance windows: 4-hour monthly window is fine; we'll specify that scheduled windows are communicated 72 hours in advance and will be excluded from availability calculations.
- Measurement: availability will be calculated using production ingress metrics; we will exclude planned rollouts flagged in the release pipeline.
- Latency: P95 <= 400ms is achievable on most of the curated model catalog for typical prompt sizes. I'll add an operational note that latency objectives will be evaluated against the model version pinned in the Order Form and for the region specified.

I will attach a draft excerpt of the Order Form addendum with operational language and measurement formulas for yours to review.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Dedicated & Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Attachment: OrderForm_Addendum_Atlas.txt (draft excerpt)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Availability target and order form language - AtlasHealth

Hi Nina — attaching the items you requested for legal review and next steps. Per your ask, we've scoped an Order Form addendum that documents a 99.95% monthly availability target for the hosted production tenant and an operational P95 performance objective (<= 400ms) tied to the model/version called out in the Order Form.

What's attached: 
- OrderForm_Draft_redlines.docx (proposed addendum + credit schedule)
- Atlas_MSA_v3.pdf (we've reviewed and included inline comments in the Order Form where necessary)

Key points in the draft (summary):
- Availability measurement: explicit formula and reporting cadence; monthly signed uptime report to be provided within 5 business days of month close.
- Credit bands and termination right described (matches Ben's commercial proposal).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (4-hour monthly window), emergency mitigations, force majeure, and customer misconfigurations.
- Latency: P95 included as a performance objective with an escalation path (incident review and remediation plan) but no automatic invoice credits.

Next steps for Atlas: please confirm whether the credit bands and termination thresholds are acceptable. Once we have alignment, we'll move to DocuSign and generate a PO-ready combined Order Form + Addendum.

I'll also include a DocuSign packet link once legal confirms their redlines.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
